summary: A JWT signing key rotation published the new key and removed the old one in a single change, so 92% of token validations failed until it was reverted. Vigil traced it to the JWKS commit fifteen minutes before the alert and named checkout as the user-facing service in the blast radius.

timeline.event: Commit e1f2a3b4c5 deployed: signing key switched to kid-2026-08, previous key dropped from config/auth/jwks.json.
TokenValidationFailures alert fired for auth (92% rejection rate).
Vigil brief posted: SEV3 with checkout in the blast radius, culprit e1f2a3b4c5 at 0.91 confidence.
Incident marked resolved after the JWKS change was reverted and CD redeployed auth.

root_cause: Key rotation is a two-step operation and shipped as one. Removing kid-2026-02 from the published key set at the same moment signing moved to kid-2026-08 meant any verifier holding a cached JWKS rejected every new token with 'unknown key id'.
contributing_factors: Verifiers cache the JWKS for 10 minutes, so the old key had to remain published across at least one cache lifetime.
No staging check validated a token signed with the new key against a cold verifier.
impact: Auth is not user facing but checkout depends on it: new sign-ins and session refreshes failed for the duration of the incident.
resolution: Reverted e1f2a3b4c5 so the previous key id was published again; CD redeployed auth and validation recovered.
went_well: The blast radius from the service graph made the customer impact obvious even though the alerting service is internal.
The deploy-config runbook prescribed the git revert path that was actually used.
went_poorly: A rotation runbook exists in principle but the two-deploy sequence was not enforced anywhere.
The change touched code and published config together, so a config-only rollback was not possible.

action_items.description: Split key rotation into publish-both then switch-signing deploys, enforced in CI.
Add a verifier smoke test that validates a freshly signed token against a cold JWKS cache.
Write an auth runbook section covering key rotation and rollback.
